author_claim: Text of edition established using Westcott and Hort as modified baseline collated against three other critical editions to identify variant readings
short_quote: The starting point for the SBLGNT was the edition of Westcott and Hort.
qualification: WH text adjusted for SBLGNT orthographic standards before comparison

author_claim: Editor defines target text as the variant that most likely reflects the earliest circulating archetype
short_quote: ...which variant most likely represents the form in which the text first began to be copied and to circulate.
qualification: Precision of editorial goal in selecting variant readings

author_claim: Single square brackets restricted to six instances in NT (including Eph 1:1 and Col 1:20) to avoid biasing decisions toward inclusion
short_quote: ...single brackets appear only six times in the SBLGNT (at Luke 22:19–20; 24:40; 24:51; 24:52; Eph 1:1; Col 1:20).
qualification: Avoids dodging editorial duty and over-inclusion bias

author_claim: Breathing marks treated as interpretive; rough breathing printed on forms of autos in select Pauline contexts
short_quote: ...the SBLGNT occasionally prints a rough breathing on forms of αὐτός.
qualification: Adopted following minority UBS committee view on reflexive sense

author_claim: In 1 Cor 12:10 editor rejects connective de across clauses adopting asyndetic reading absent from all four reference editions
short_quote: 10 ⸀ἄλλῳ Holmes ] + δὲ WH Treg NIV RP
qualification: One of 56 variation units where editor departs from all four primary editions

author_claim: Where Westcott and Hort printed consecutive punctuation marks in Pastoral Epistles editor reduced them to a single mark
short_quote: Where Westcott and Hort employed two consecutive punctuation marks... these have been reduced to a single mark.
qualification: Punctuation otherwise adheres generally to WH

author_claim: Where modern paragraph breaks conflict with WH punctuation decisions are made on a case-by-case contextual basis
short_quote: ...at the end of Phil 1:18, WH’s punctuation was given preference over the NRSV paragraph break...
qualification: Phil 1:18 favors WH punctuation; Phil 2:14 favors NRSV break

author_claim: Editor departs from BDAG orthographic guideline in Col 2:16 printing noumenias instead of neomenias
short_quote: A rare exception to the guideline is the adoption of νουμηνίας rather than νεομηνίας in Col 2:16.
qualification: Explicitly noted exception to general BDAG standard
